loci.exact: ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν Ὠσηὲ μετονομάζει Μωυσῆς εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν (Num. 13,17), τὸν ποιὸν εἰς ἕξιν μεταχαράττων. Ὠσηὲ μὲν γὰρ ἑρμηνεύεται ποιὸς οὗτος, Ἰησοῦς δὲ σωτηρία κυρίου, ἕξεως ὄνομα τῆς ἀρίστης.
loci.gloss: Moses renames Hosea Jesus, re-stamping a quality into a state; Ἰησοῦς is glossed 'salvation of the Lord', the name of the best state. No Logos at this locus.

loci.exact: οὕτω μετεχαράχθη καὶ τὸ τοῦ λεχθέντος νόμισμα πρὸς ἰδέαν βελτίονα.
loci.gloss: the renaming as the re-striking of a coin to a better form (cf. #642, #1458).

loci.exact: ἤκουσα μέντοι καὶ τῶν Μωυσέως ἑταίρων τινὸς ἀποφθεγξαμένου τοιόνδε λόγιον· „ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος ᾧ ὄνομα ἀνατολή„ (Zach. 6, 12)
loci.gloss: the oracle of Zechariah 6:12, put in the mouth of 'one of the companions of Moses' (the phrase the 2025-11-09 Chariot Companion commentary turns on).

loci.exact: ἐὰν δὲ τὸν ἀσώματον ἐκεῖνον, θείας ἀδιαφοροῦντα εἰκόνος, ὁμολογήσεις ὅτι εὐθυβολώτατον ὄνομα ἐπεφημίσθη τὸ ἀνατολῆς αὐτῷ·
loci.gloss: the man named Anatole read as the incorporeal one, no different from the divine image.

loci.exact: τοῦτον μὲν γὰρ πρεσβύτατον υἱὸν ὁ τῶν ὅλων ἀνέτειλε πατήρ, ὃν ἑτέρωθι πρωτόγονον ὠνόμασε,
loci.gloss: that man is the eldest son, elsewhere named the firstborn.

loci.exact: κατὰ τὸν πρωτόγονον αὐτοῦ λόγον, τὸν ἀγγέλων πρεσβύτατον, ὡς ἂν ἀρχάγγελον, πολυώνυμον ὑπάρχοντα· καὶ γὰρ ἀρχὴ καὶ ὄνομα θεοῦ καὶ λόγος καὶ ὁ κατ’ εἰκόνα ἄνθρωπος καὶ ὁ ὁρῶν, Ἰσραήλ, προσαγορεύεται.
loci.gloss: the firstborn is the Logos, many-named: beginning, name of God, logos, the man after the image.

loci.exact: Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ἰωσεδὲκ τοῦ ἱερέως τοῦ μεγάλου
loci.gloss: the verse before the oracle: the crowns set on the head of Ἰησοῦς son of Iosedek, the high priest. The seated line carries apparatus text run into it (a seat defect, flagged below).

loci.exact: Ἰδοὺ ἀνήρ, Ἀνατολὴ ὄνομα αὐτῷ, καὶ ὑποκάτωθεν αὐτοῦ ἀνατελεῖ, καὶ οἰκοδομήσει τὸν οἶκον Κυρίου·
loci.gloss: the oracle Philo quotes; the man named Anatole is the Ἰησοῦς of 6:11.

findings: The post of 2025-10-19 quotes Philo: 'The name Jesus (Ἰησοῦς) is the name of the Logos' (De Mutatione Nominum §121–123), and attributes a Joshua–Logos sentence to Life of Moses II.114–132. Neither sentence is in the seated Cohn–Wendland text. Mut. 121–123 glosses Ἰησοῦς as 'salvation of the Lord, the name of the best state' and carries no Logos; Vit. Mos. II.114–132 carries no Joshua (it treats the high priest's vestments and the twofold logos). The post stays as published; the piece states what the seated texts carry.

Philo identifies the Logos with the man of Zechariah 6:12, whose name is Anatole (Conf. 62–63, 146). In the LXX the verse before (Zech 6:11) crowns Ἰησοῦς son of Iosedek, the high priest, and 6:12 names him. Philo quotes 6:12 alone: the name rides in the verse, unsaid by Philo. That 6:11 is in his view is an inference, stated as one.

The oracle comes from 'one of the companions of Moses' (τῶν Μωυσέως ἑταίρων τινός, Conf. 62). The Chariot Companion commentary (2025-11-09) turns on that phrase and says Philo 'did not leave us names'; at Conf. 62 the companion is Zechariah and what he utters is the Anatole oracle.
Mut. 121–123 carries the renaming as a re-stamping (μεταχαράττων; τὸ τοῦ λεχθέντος νόμισμα), the vocabulary of #642 and #1458.

The Sapphic channel in Philo is the subject of #1486 (Mut. 54–57, Her. 3–4, Migr. 47–48) and of #1458 (Philo beside Longinus). With the above, one author carries both the transform and the Logos-as-the-crowned-Ἰησοῦς: the join the genetic reading has to make across authors everywhere else.
seat_flags: lxx-swete Zechariah 3:8 and 6:11: apparatus text is run into the verse lines (the OCR layer). 3:8's Ἀνατολήν cannot be asserted from the seat; 6:11's Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ἰωσεδὲκ can. A repair of the seat, in its own commit.
owed: external scholarship on Philo's Logos and Zechariah 6:12 (Conf. 62–63, 146), on Mut. 121, and on Philo's names for the Logos, publicly obtainable only (the commons stance)
